description: OpenCode custom-provider block + turn watchdog (Abilityai/lilu#257 step 6, the DGX-Ollama path). The provider half asserts the emitted `opencode.json` VERBATIM, because the failure mode is silent: a misshapen `provider.ollama` does not crash, it makes OpenCode fall back to its own default model on a turn the operator believes is running locally. `runtime: {type: opencode, model: "ollama/gemma4:12b"}` plus OPENCODE_OLLAMA_BASE_URL is sufficient on its own — the pinned model is always declared, so nobody maintains a parallel model list to use the model they already pinned; OPENCODE_OLLAMA_MODELS adds the extras. Base URL normalisation is idempotent (an operator who wrote /v1 does not get /v1/v1) and a non-http(s) value fails with a NAMED reason carrying the env var (quality bar 6), never a silent skip that degrades into OpenCode's own "unknown provider". Unset base URL emits no `provider` key at all, so the Anthropic/OpenRouter agent is untouched (graceful degradation); a foreign provider's model can never leak into the ollama model map; an operator-declared block wins on npm/options while its models are UNIONED, so a customised config can never be missing the model the turn was launched with; other providers survive the merge. The wiring is proven on disk through `_prepare_turn_config`, not just in the pure function. The watchdog half pins F6: the window before the first `step_start` is SILENT and was measured at 7.2s–59.3s for byte-identical configs on a real DGX (the variance is the provider's own model load), so the 300s default is ~5x the worst measured floor and is clamped to never exceed the turn timeout; a bad override falls back rather than disabling, because '0 means off' would let a typo remove the protection. A stall gets exactly ONE retry on a FRESH session (resuming the wedged session would reproduce the wedge) reusing the execution_id so the ledger shows one execution, not a phantom pair; a second stall is 504 and NEVER a success; a non-stall failure is not retried, since re-running a 500 would double every real error. The `step_start` event name is asserted against the real v1.18.32 stream — a rename would make the watchdog kill every healthy turn.
